items.q: What goes wrong when a leader asks 'are we on track?' and you dump project context?
items.a: Status checks want **one sentence**, not every wireframe delay. Over-detail reads as **unclear and hard to follow**, not thorough. Fix with **ACQ**: Answer → Context → Question.

items.q: When does thinking out loud hurt your credibility?
items.a: Externalizing the full **decision tree** is fine in brainstorming; in decision moments leaders want the **final version**, not the rough draft. Pause, take a thinker pose, then deliver the **decision** via ACQ.

sections.title: Take a position without being difficult

items.q: Why does 'I'm easy / whatever works' make you forgettable?
items.a: **Neutrality ≠ flexibility** — it signals a **lack of decisiveness**. People stop asking for your opinion and you become irrelevant. Fix with **PRO**: Position → Reason → Open.

items.q: Is mirroring the room enough in high-stakes meetings?
items.a: Rapport needs **match first**, but only mirroring never guides. Practice **energy leadership**: read → match/mirror → gradually **shift** volume, warmth, and melody so you lead the room.

items.q: Which voice habits silently flatten your influence?
items.a: Same **rate, volume, and melody** every time means you play maybe five keys. Treat voice as an **88-key instrument**: rate for passion vs weight, volume for confidence vs lean-in, melody for engagement — dials anyone can learn.
